title: What shoes should you wear for lifting? (Flat sole vs high heel)
summary: NH wears heeled Olympic weightlifting shoes for all knee-flexion (squat) work and thin-soled, flat, high-ankle shoes for everything else, especially pulls from the floor. He gives two rules for buying shoes (sole as wide or wider at the toes than the heel, and a straight, not banana-curved, sole), notes that flat shoes suit low-bar squatters or very mobile people, and advises against lifting barefoot because gyms may ban it.

claims.claim: NH wears heeled Olympic weightlifting shoes for any knee-flexion movement (all squats) and flat, thin-soled, high-ankle shoes for everything else.
Weightlifting shoes give more squat depth and open the hips by effectively adding ankle flexibility.
NH can squat to depth without them, but given his history of knee pain the shoes helped him work through it, so he always squats in them.
Good weightlifting shoes are heavy and grippy, making you feel anchored and stable on the floor.

Rule 1: the sole should be as wide or wider at the toes than at the heel; most commercial shoes are wide at the heel and narrow at the toes, which is unnatural, scrunches the toes and prevents you from anchoring.

Don't pull from the floor (deadlifts, rows) in heeled shoes: the heel adds a deficit, making you bend over more and lengthening the range of motion. Olympic weightlifters are an exception since they clean in them.
Rule 2: the sole must be straight, not curved like a banana; banana-soled sneakers roll the ankles in, causing knee cave, losing the posterior chain and glutes, ruining posture and risking injury.
He likes his flat shoes because they have almost no sole, so they add no deficit to his deadlift.
People who prefer flat shoes like Chuck Taylors for squatting usually have exceptional hip and ankle mobility or squat low bar, which involves more hip hinge and posterior chain.
High-bar squatters will usually prefer heeled shoes because high bar is more of a knee-flexion movement needing maximal ankle mobility.
Avoid sneakers and Jordans for lifting; they're fine for curls if you want to show them off.

Lifting barefoot is great (NH used to), but gyms may ban it as a liability, and if you get used to barefoot deadlifts and are then forced into shoes you could lose about 40 lb on your pull; find a good shoe you can wear anywhere.
